text:
A strange little place... Maybe that island truly exists, maybe it's a mirage, a phantasm, a glamour. The island is covered in thick forests and deep bogs. All sorts of creatures live there, some intelligent, some you couldn't really call that. I saw kikimoras, satyrs, I even saw a talking fox! And above all — there are hordes of ghosts there! Kanians mostly, sort of alive and sort of not. And they all obey the mistress of the place — Ziva, I think she's called — whether she's a woman, a bird, or some kind of spirit altogether. A peaceful place; the mistress was kind to us that time, gave us rest and shelter. Only I've heard from other travelers that some misfortune befell it recently — an unhappy love, or some curse... In short, I'd think twice before mooring at Iriy without holy water and loaded cannons.

Bosses: Bosk, Mister and Missus, Naiad, Marena.

The ancient city-state of Dersaadet is a true historical monument. Its beautiful squares and palaces keep the spirit of long-gone times.

This is exactly how the cities of the Xadagan Empire looked in that memorable time when the heroes of "Evil Islands" walked their streets.

Lost in the Astral, Dersaadet escaped the demon invasion and any part in the bloody war of the great factions. The local Xadaganians have never seen a mana pipeline and do not know Yasker, yet they cannot be called savages.

Any local architect could outdo the best masters of Sarnaut, and the grace of its maidens would make even elven dancers envious!

Alas, life prepared a cruel trial for the last sultan of Dersaadet. His only daughter would die on the day she came of age, poisoned by a snake's venom — so a Gypsy woman foretold. Unwilling to accept his fate, the ruler built an unreachable tower and hid his child in it. But on the girl's eighteenth birthday a sinister magical haze enveloped her refuge. The green mist took the shape of a huge snake coiled around the tower walls.

Soon rumors spread from the palace square that some misfortune had befallen the princess and that the lawful ruler of the city had vanished. Taking advantage of this, the unruly janizaries began to plunder the city they had sworn to protect.

It is said that behind it all stands the cunning Vizier — a great wizard and master of transformation.

Rumor has it that he isn't even a man, but a jinn who has taken mortal form. One way or another, traveling heroes will certainly have to face this powerful and domineering figure if they wish to shed light on the island's dark mystery.

For now the future of Dersaadet is hidden in mist even from the strongest oracles. Who knows, perhaps it is your party that will manage to get into the princess's tower? Whether you can save the unfortunate girl and win the coveted reward for it depends on you alone!

Bosses: Minotaur, Mehmet Pasha, Rajima, Lamia Princess.

Aha, I know that place. A gloomy little spot, I must say. Once there was a circus there, the most ordinary circus, with clowns, acrobats and a trained bear with a balalaika. But the place wasn't popular. Who would fly through the perilous Astral just to look at some jesters? And so the circus fell into complete ruin.

And then three men turned up there, calling themselves professors, specialists in dreams and fantasies. They patched up the old circus buildings and sent invitations to their Carnival to anyone who wanted one. The masters of the Carnival guarantee the fulfillment of the most secret desires, the most rosy dreams and the most incredible fantasies.

If you ask me, they're charlatans through and through. They don't take money from anyone, by the way, which is really strange. Now, if they wanted to line their pockets, the point of such promises would at least be clear. For now, all I can advise you is — keep your wits about you!

Bosses: Dread, Heat, Red Beard, Harlequin.

Thinking of joining the Historians, are you? Any Historian would give his right hand without a second thought to explore Koch-Itzmahl.

Just imagine — a fully preserved temple from the heyday of the June empire. Not those pitiful ruins scattered everywhere, but a complete temple complex.

I confess I only glimpsed it, and even so I nearly fell overboard in amazement! Bas-reliefs, frescoes, statues, carved columns... Ah, and how many secrets it hides, how many treasures... Only there's no way to get at them!

Lizards have overrun the whole island. When we tried to land, they pelted us with spears, burned a huge hole in the sail with a fireball, and kept promising to tear out our hearts and lay them on the altar of their ancestors. Their chief, Shisskh, raged most of all. Ooh, vicious creatures!

We had to turn round urgently and move on empty-handed.

Clearing the temple of the lizards' presence is a good deed and pleasing to the Light... and a profitable one besides!

Bosses: Caiman, Lion, Bloodberry, Shisskh the Seven-Fingered.

Don't you know? "Where to? To East Overshoe!" — that's how merchants used to answer anyone too curious before casting off from the pier. And not without reason — on East Overshoe there was a rich trading town whose inhabitants, you might say, spoke in nothing but sayings. Whatever you asked a local, he'd answer you with a proverb.

A rich town it was, and misfortune passed it by. The townsfolk got so used to a quiet life that they would say, "we'll start shutting the gates when the crayfish whistles on the mountain." Well, the crayfish held out and held out, and then it whistled. They got what they asked for. And they had been told — let sleeping trouble lie!

I flew past East Overshoe the other day — everything has fallen into desolation, not a sound, not a rustle. But who knows what is really going on there? From afar it's just an abandoned town, but, as they say, still waters run deep!

Bosses: Sleeping Trouble, Clop, Byak and Zyrk, the Noon Witch, Raak.

Frost and cold — that's all I can say about Kyoltmark. I've never been there myself, but I know that one of the first gibberling ships was wrecked on that icy rock. When, a few years later, League ships finally found the rock, the surviving gibberlings had already settled on that miserable scrap of land, made themselves at home and flatly refused to leave the island that had become their home.

But not long ago disaster struck — astral demons attacked the island. And strangest of all, they didn't slaughter the inhabitants but took them captive. They say a mighty demon named the Thought Catcher turned all the gibberlings into his slaves, and now they serve him loyally and devotedly. A terrible fate!

If you find yourself on that island, you won't be able to avoid fighting the maddened gibberlings. Strike without pity — only empty shells remain of the locals, and the demons control their will!

Bosses: Fiend, Guur'Maan, Sharpclaw, Thought Catcher.

I suppose you already know that many achievements of imperial magic and science owe their existence to closed secret laboratories?

However, there is a dark stain in the chronicle of these glorious deeds. I'm talking about Lab Nine.

Yasskul Setnakhte, a cultist of Tep who knew his master's work firsthand, disrupted the course of important experiments and recreated a terrible disease — the Plague that wiped out the Zem people.

Now the victims of this disease rule the island unchallenged. There is no way to cure them. Only one thing remains — to grant peace both to them and to the head of Lab Nine, General Zubin, who is now called nothing but "General Plague." The infected zombies that carry the disease must also be destroyed. And of course Yasskul Setnakhte himself — the cause of all the plague island's woes — deserves to die. Are you up to this feat?

Bosses: General Plague, Stonecutter, Yasskul Setnakhte.

Far out in the Astral I once happened upon an island where eternal winter reigns. It is ruled by Yaver Arteia, a mad Arisen woman who calls herself the Snow Queen. Oh, what a vile hag she is, I tell you! I escaped from that island by a sheer miracle. The Snow Queen's favorite pastime is to abduct people and set them all manner of riddles. Fail to guess one, and you are turned into an ice statue! In her ice castle Yaver Arteia keeps whole galleries of ice sculptures that were once orcs, gibberlings, Arisen, humans... Her heart is as cold as her icy throne!

That merciless shrew was all set to turn me into an ice statue, and only by a miracle did I get away.

Yaver Arteia must be stopped! If she simply killed people, fine — you'd rest a while in Purgatory, and that's that. But she turns them into statues. Just imagine: a man stands there, unable to move, to breathe, even to close his eyes. And so for a year, two, ten... Brr, how horrible. No, such cold-blooded torment cannot go unpunished!

But reaching the queen will not be easy. Chill, a mad werebear shaman, faithfully guards his mistress's peace. And rumor has it that in especially fierce blizzards a huge bear named Helad appears on the island — though whether that is true, it will be up to you to find out.

Bosses: Helad, Sharptooth, Chill, Yaver Arteia.

For as long as I've been sailing the Astral, this little island was always just a frozen rock — no life, no vegetation. But recently it was transformed as if by magic — now there are streams flowing and trees blooming, and even some little houses standing there! I moored at the shore, and more wonders — creatures live there such as I've never seen in my life. Like gibberlings, but not gibberlings, fluffy and big-eared. They're friendly and hospitable, only somehow skittish. They say another tribe lives beyond the mountains, and they fear their kin might make war on them. I wished them the Light's help, and they gave me a strange look and sent me on my way. A riddle, not an island, honest to goodness!

Bosses: Li-Ter, Plamennik, Fluffy, Claire Brightley.
Bosses: Rustle, Burian Jagger and Gurrian Jagger, Yarosvat Zoriev, Porfiry Polenov.

This rich mine belonged until recently to Umoir merchants. That is, they thought it belonged to them — but in truth the Mistress still lives in the depths of the island to this day. If she wishes, she shares her riches; if she doesn't, she sends misfortune. Well, she stopped wishing. Whether people angered her with their greed or failed to show her respect, only now wolves and bears roam the village instead of miners. I wouldn't fly there: what if the Mistress gets angry with me too! Her riches in the depths are countless, of course — but she guards them so that you can't get near!

Bosses: Fire Jumper, Blue Yaga, Mighty Poloz, Mistress of the Copper Mountain.

Many have heard stories about the Silent Hills. An ancient evil awoke in that land, turning the peasants into will-less ghosts. They wandered their lands until brave heroes put an end to their suffering.

But in the deep layers of the Astral the Silent Hills have a reflection. It was this that an imperial Warlock chose for his experiments. And he got so carried away that the horrors of old now seem like a children's fairy tale. The villain destroyed the whole people and turned the good inhabitants into an army of the undead. Those hills are Silent no longer, but Dead!

Bosses: Cadaver, Guardian, Murderess, Sarang Fravashi.
Bosses: Negus Mengulis, Rowdy Raja, Bubbah Two Fingers, Gire the Merciless.

Ah, the Aoidoi. They've only just been introduced, and they've already built cities — for everyone to see. New Bay is only just being built, but it will be a splendid city! You can't deny these stone-heads their courage, of course — the sector where the Bay stands is literally teeming with crazed monsters. Let's hope no misfortune comes of it... I've heard, by the way, that some demons don't want to fight them but are offering friendship. Hogwash, if you ask me. If the Aoidoi trust those creatures, they're as naive as children.

Bosses: Agniy, Datura, Vile, Or-Khan.

A distant and inaccessible cloister — the dream of every bachelor in Sarnaut. And no wonder, since this allod is inhabited exclusively by maidens, every one of them clever and beautiful. Seekers of romantic adventure should be careful, though. The beauties fled to Fenia's Cloister in search of a calm and quiet life, so they welcome guests very reluctantly.

Bosses: Lagoda Vereskova, Softpaw, Poleaxe the Merciless, Fenia.
Bosses: Hestia, Bedlam, Blinder, Diamond.

The former inhabitants of Altan Tepek are long dead, but deep within the city abandoned mechanisms keep on working.

Bosses: Frostmount, Jasper Defender, Metztlitotec, Ayateotle.

What questions you ask! I'd gladly forget that island, but I can't...

Long ago Kanian druids brought a shoot of the Great Tree to a lifeless islet and turned the barren stone into a truly magnificent forest. I happened to visit it, and I confess without a word of a lie — even in the Empire there are few places whose beauty could compare with that wonderful sunny island as it was then. The mentor of the local pagans, the wise Dobroslav Radov, proved a most cordial Host and welcomed me, an Imperial, hospitably, not caring a jot about all the disagreements between our powers! I left the island with a friendly farewell and warm memories of birdsong, crystal-clear lakes, the most delicious birch sap and the rustle of thick foliage.

And recently bad news reached me. A giant spider, a vile spawn of the Astral, crept up to the Great Tree under cover of darkness and poisoned it with its venom. All of Dobroslav's followers, and he himself, went mad. Now he is called Zlobinya Yadov, and nothing remains in him of the good-natured sage he once was. Now he and his servants offer blood sacrifices to the Desecrated Tree! The whole island is overrun with venomous spiders tirelessly spawned by their mother, Widixa. And Blackvenom himself hides somewhere in the thick forest. But if you tear out the hearts of the mad pagans and grant them peace by burning them in cleansing fire, Blackvenom will surely not be slow to appear. And with his death the blight will leave the forest forever.

I beg you, cleanse the Desecrated Forest! Kill the Widow and Blackvenom, and perhaps the soul of the one I remember by the name of Dobroslav will find peace...

Bosses: Widixa, Zlobinya Yadov, Yevstigney Volkov, Blackvenom.

The island is a waterfolk village in the jungle, with an altar in the center. There is a map.

To make the boss appear, you have to collect 10 bodies for the sacrifice from the waterfolk's cauldrons and lay them on the altar; there are 10 cauldrons in all, so a single character has to do the collecting. The cauldrons are scattered around the center, so to collect them you'll have to make a circuit of the island; the last two cauldrons are to the left and right of the altar.

Bosses: Waterfolk Priest, Gavial, Serket.

What do you think of goblins?

On the one hand — pitiful creatures. Everyone laughs at them and despises them a little. They are the heroes of countless jokes and the pets of orc shamans. Sometimes you simply feel sorry for them.

And on the other hand? Thieves and bandits. Mischief-makers, always ready to do something vile. Ever had dealings with the arms mafia on the Coba Plateau? There you go!

There is a goblin island in the Astral. Their stronghold. A Republic! They even elect one of those, what's it called... such a funny word... a president! For three terms in a row now a shaman named Urub has been elected that very president. It is he who organizes the goblins' pirate raids.

If in your wanderings you manage to find that island — carry out the sentence and behead the goblin republic!

Bosses: Goblin Overseer, Buzz, Urub.

I've never had occasion to visit the Edge island.

It got its name because it often appears near the Holy Land. No wonder the League and the Empire sought to seize it to use as an additional base. Our side proved quicker.

But now access to the island is forbidden. The Xadaganian garrison defending the Edge has betrayed the Empire! Evidently there were demon cultists among them who managed to cloud the soldiers' minds. Or perhaps the whole thing is down to the astral worm that has dug in in the middle of the island. They say it can have a destructive effect on the mind.

Elizaveta Rysina herself recently summoned me and questioned me about the heroes of the Empire. The thing is, our side currently has no way to send a punitive expedition to the island. And yet the traitors must be punished! And the island cleansed of demons!

Bosses: Cultist Captain, Garm, Astral Worm.

Do you know the story of the Isle of the Damned? No? It's a story about how the Darkness in the soul is more terrible than the Darkness outside.

On a distant island lost in the Astral there was a small village. Good people lived there, honest and hard-working. And among them were two young lovers, Ivan and Marya. When the time came, they were wed, all properly and decently, and began to live happily and prosper. That's where the fairy tale should end... Only you and I don't live in a fairy tale.

There was a man in that village, an outsider. A bad, envious man. He couldn't calmly watch the newlyweds' happiness and Marya's beauty — he was terribly jealous of Ivan.

And he decided to destroy the young couple. By deceit he got hold of Marya's wedding ring, a love letter and the bride's bouquet, which had stayed unwithered ever since the wedding, and with the help of these things he laid a terrible curse on the young couple.

Because of that curse both young people soon went to their graves. Only the evil did not go unpunished: the curse fell upon the whole island, and the villain himself was not spared by it. He died and turned into vicious undead.

And the souls of the young couple remained restless. There is no bright path for them while the curse lies upon them. To lift it, you will first have to find the ring, the letter and the flowers the villain used for the curse, bring them to the young couple's grave, and then set the souls free.

Bosses: Heartbreaker, Shishimora, Korosten, Ivan Neladov and Maria Neladova.

If you open a primer at the letter "K" (for krepost, "fortress"), you can see a fortress surrounded by a sturdy stone wall. That picture appeared long, long ago, and as his model the artist used the Hunters' Stockade — an exemplary defensive structure of those times. It was built before the Cataclysm, when the Abatis Line was being laid — a long chain of fortifications against orc raids.

After the catastrophe the fortress vanished into the Astral along with other shards of the old world.

Bosses: Blitzkrieg, Zugunder, Paunch, Kaput.

A passion for destruction is an extremely dangerous passion. The consequences can be especially tragic if the desire to destroy everything flares up in the heart of an outstanding person. You can see this once again on the allod of Cinderland — once a luxurious hunting preserve of the Empire.

Of the former grandeur and beauty of this place only the charred skeletons of huge trees remain as a reminder. Fire has swallowed the whole island, turning the allod into a living monument to the terrible experiments of a Great Mage.

Bosses: Kuzmich, Oakwarden, Volkh, Fireborn.

That place is well known — it has an evil reputation all over the Astral. The foremost pirate nest in the world! What bandits and cutthroats aren't there! Feint the Greedy himself moved there not long before his death — they say he buried his treasure there too... Well, anyone is quick to wag his tongue about pirate hoards. But the fresh rumors about that island are much worse. They say someone has finally found a way to deal with the buccaneers. A gentleman of fortune I know wanted to stop there and sell off his loot, only he looks — smoke billowing, the fort in ruins, and above it something like bluish tentacles as thick as a mast swaying... In short, a decent person had no business there before, and now even less so!

Bosses: Badyai, Merry, Shroud Weaver, Kraken.

For a long time nobody knew whether the Underwater Kingdom really existed, or whether it was just the invention of liars and dreamers telling tales of some tiny islet lost in the Astral with nothing on it but a wooden hut and a well.

At first glance it may seem there's nothing interesting there, and at second glance too. But it is precisely on this islet that the only entrance to the underwater kingdom of the sea lord lies. I wonder what riches are hidden beneath the depths?

Kanian skalds love to sing the song of a mighty sweet-voiced knight who not only visited the underwater city but was generously rewarded by the sea lord himself. Whether it was so or not, one can only guess. Or else visit the underwater kingdom and find out everything for yourself.

Bosses: Bereginya, Goldfeather Fish, Blackmarin, Sea King.

Countess Yasskul Bathory, once the most beautiful of Hickut's rulers, seized on every chance to regain her lost beauty. Unfortunately, she managed to find an effective means of rejuvenation — using the blood of young girls.

It is said the Blood Countess has taken refuge on one of the astral islands. There she has a whole manor with well-drilled and devoted servants. The horrors and debauchery going on in her domain would drive even a battle-hardened warrior mad. But Bathory chose a picturesque, even pleasant, spot. At first glance you would never guess that some evil could be lurking here.

Bosses: Yaver Nadashti, Rolling Hill, Mechanical Watchman, Yasskul Bathory.

And how do you know about that, eh?

That's classified information! The Committee will wring your neck for divulging it!

Oh, all right. Since you already know about the heretics themselves, so be it — I'll share it with you in secret. But mind you, not a word to anyone!

The Heretic Refuge is a stain on the reputation of all the Arisen. After all, it is from their people that all these dangerous madmen come!

The heretics refuse to recognize the holiness of Nezeb, Tensess and Skrakan. They believe that all that exists arose from four elements — fire, earth, water, and nature as the union of all three pure elements. And they have grown so hidebound in their heresy that they accept no arguments of reason. They fiercely hate everyone who does not share their faith. After several high-profile murders committed by this sect, the Church, with the full support of the Committee and of Yasker himself, anathematized them and opened a hunt for them.

The heretics — or rather, the handful that was left of their sect — seized an astral ship in port and vanished into the depths of the Astral. Time passed, and their existence was simply forgotten; all the documents were classified and handed over to the archive. And not long ago a captain I know told me he had heard about the heretics from someone who had seen with his own eyes a man who had the misfortune to stumble upon their refuge in the Astral. That poor wretch barely escaped! His ship was scorched by fire, a gaping hole from a huge boulder yawned in the hold, all the rigging was covered in mold, and half the crew had turned into ice statues...

So if your adventures lead you to the secret refuge of the heretics, know this — they are mad killers, and they will try to destroy you at any cost!

Bosses: Yasskul Flach, Negus Minhotep, Negus Haifa, Negus Zirach.
Bosses: Mamba, Capa, Twisthorn, Nastasya Zhmurova.

I had a friend — Roman Kuzin. A traveler, an explorer. And ill luck carried him to the Lost Isle. There's been no word from him since...

The Lost Isle is a legend. The legend of Tep's Pyramid, which acquired a mind of its own and stamps out undead, placing Sparks into dead bodies. It is known that whoever manages to defeat the Pyramid will get a treasure.

That is exactly what Romka dreamed of. He gathered information about the island. I'll tell it to you if you undertake to find this island and rescue my comrade.

On the Lost Isle you will meet magical elementals that embody the Pyramid's power. You will meet many undead it has created. By destroying them you will be able to reach the Pyramid itself, where you must find a way to shut it down. And if you do that and the Pyramid stops working, its treasure will be your reward.

Well? Will you take on the job?

Bosses: ver. 1: Pulsating Magic Elemental, Cobweb Spider, Pyramid Guardian.

ver. 2: Pulsating Magic Elemental, Cobweb Spider, Zinoviy Semetry, Pyramid Guardian.

The seasons... Once, before the Cataclysm, these words meant something more than just a change of dates on the calendar. The seasons followed one another without the help of mages, and there was nothing more constant in the whole world. But the old Sarnaut shattered into thousands of shards — and with it many of the orders of the old world vanished.

Bosses: Winter, Spring the Fair, Autumn the Woeful, Bright Summer.

Looking for treasure, are you? Heh-heh... There's no treasure there! Only sand, the scorching sun, heat, and scorpions nesting among the ruins.

As a Historian I know told me, there was once a huge observatory there, in which the June priests studied the movement of the sun and stars and compiled solar and lunar calendars and the most detailed horoscopes. And now all that's left of the temple-observatory are ruins half buried in sand.

And not long ago the Wormfaces returned to the Tlalkoa Ruins. They cleared some of the halls, repaired the old battle golems and jealously guard the ruins against any intrusion. Their leader, who, as I understood, is called Mirage, desperately needs something in those ruins, and he will kill without hesitation anyone who enters beneath the vaults of the old temple. Luckily I got away in time, or my bones too would be drying in the hot desert sun now...

Bosses: Isides, Rattler, Horatrix, Mirage.

Imperials love to boast of their technology and to play at conquering nature. That is why they placed one of their secret sanatoriums not just anywhere, but in the midst of the eternal ice. They found a suitable islet, frozen to its very core. They raised a dome there, and inside it built a fine, cozy little town. Outside the blizzard howls, but inside all is bliss — birds sing and the grass is green.

Only during construction they didn't take into account that a tribe of wild orcs lives in the caves under the dome. And that would have been fine, but in the course of the work they poured concrete over some important underground stream. Without water, first the mountain goats died, then the mushrooms in the caves dried up. The orcs went hungry and began coming out of the caves and attacking the sanatorium's guards. And the guards there are fierce — veterans to a man. The secrecy is of the highest level, which is why all outsiders are shot on the spot.

Bosses: Shakhrai-Gor, Pavel Syrin, Vyacheslav Lapochkin, Alexander Burdakin.

Don't even ask. You're not supposed to know about this island, and neither am I. It's secret, se-cret, what's not to understand? Oh, all right, I'll whisper what I know. Some experiments were carried out there with the technologies captured in the Dead City. Where they wanted to open the gates, I don't know, and where they did open them, I don't want to know. Why? Because the other day the personnel were urgently evacuated from there, and the whole region was marked on the maps as quarantined and strictly forbidden to visit. Want to poke your nose into military secrets? Well, you do love a risk — maybe you'll find something out... No, don't tell me, I don't want to know! Although... Well, maybe in a low voice, in my ear.

Bosses: Hugger, Consumption, Rotgulp, Pandemician.

Have you ever heard of Volcano Isle? No? Then listen. Not long ago a tribe of draconids appeared on this island, worshipping a fire god who sleeps in the crater of a long-extinct volcano. With constant sacrifices the draconids kept him asleep, so that he would not awaken and his scorching fury would not break loose. But not long ago their high priest broke with custom and summoned the sleeper. The volcano awoke, and a mighty fire elemental burst out. From tongues of flame and the heat of flowing magma he created four guardians — huge fiery manticores whose breath can burn anyone to ashes on the spot! If you decide to go to the island and try to awaken the sleeping flame, you must repeat the draconids' ritual, laying the fiery hearts of shellbacks on the sacrificial altars. But don't even try to take him on while his faithful manticores are alive! The fire god put a particle of his power into each guardian, and with their deaths he will be greatly weakened. That's all I know about Volcano Isle. Good luck to you!

Bosses: Supreme Draconid, Bonesnapper, Hephaesto.
Bosses: Levoxia, Ligea, Cock Pit, Molpa.

A quiet little island, an inconspicuous one. Seven bogatyr brothers lived there, whiling away their old age among forests and bogs. Then some run-down elven House settled there — they had fled persecution on Umoir. Only they found no happiness there. First the Blight reached the island, then the head of the House brought a little gift for his wife — a Kanian woman, by the way. A wondrous mirror, a work of the ancient June — a golden frame, and the mirror itself of black obsidian. Well, June treasures are like that: from them you can only expect some trick or curse. In short, there was no reason to call at that island before, and now it's downright frightening. Although... what if there are hunters willing to get that mirror? For the bold, as everyone knows, no law is written!

Bosses: Baba Yaga, Yelisseus, Annette de Tristesse, Evil Mirror.

Aha! That story caught your interest too?

There used to be an imperial mine of ours there. Hundreds of goblins, under the watchful supervision and loud cursing of foremen, mined valuable strategic raw materials there! Well, there were also some natives who lived in the caves, kobolds and miners, but by special order of the Committee, number... oh, I can't remember, 123\16-BIS I think, all the natives were made honorary citizens of the Empire and obliged to work for the good of the country.

And those rascals didn't want to work! No notion of discipline. No faith in a bright future! Idlers!

They conspired with one very clever goblin — Ghim the Greedy is his name — won the trolls over to their side, and drove out all the foremen, engineers and bookkeepers! Now they've got some sort of monarchy or commune there, with Ghim in charge. He's blocked all the tunnels, raked a pile of gold for himself and sits there chuckling — he's beaten the Empire, if you please, the scoundrel.

But every dog has its day! There are still goblins loyal to the Empire on the island, a squad of Boomer demolitionists. They'll blast a tunnel through any rock! With their help you'll easily reach the lair of that separatist and plunderer of the people's economy, the Greedy one.

Whatever treasure you find is yours. And on behalf of the whole working class give Ghim a severe reprimand entered into his skull. The Empire will not forget you!

Bosses: Wick, Stakh Quickpick, Stonegnawer, Ghim the Greedy.

Last year's snow was falling…

Bosses: Hut, Snezhana Zaykina, Bewitched Peasant, Veres.

At the dawn of astronavigation, when there were no visors yet and the first ships moved through the Astral almost by feel, lighthouses were built on the islands that were discovered. A lighthouse's light could be seen from very far away, and it signaled: "Sail here, it's safe here." Many sailors lost in the Astral thanked fate more than once for a lighthouse glimpsed in the distance.

Later, as astronavigation developed, the role of lighthouses became less important. With a modern visor, astrolabe and navigator it's practically impossible to get lost in the Astral. And so lighthouses now are mostly a tribute to tradition and a place where you can rest in peace, spend the night and hear the latest news.

But recently I received unpleasant news — a band of astral pirates has seized one of the old lighthouses and is using it as a trap. As soon as a ship heading for the lighthouse's light moors at the pier, it is immediately boarded, plundered and smashed to splinters, and the whole crew is sent to walk the plank into the Astral!

Beasts! Barbarians! So many innocent people have suffered because of them. They must be stopped at any cost! And the treasure, if you find it, take for yourself — the dead have no use for it anymore...

Bosses: Zavid Ushkuynikov, Yasskul "Jolly" Roger, Sturdy Door, Feint the Greedy.

The island of the Silent Hills always served me as proof that in the future we and the Kanians could live in peace. I didn't often go there, but when I did, I talked without fear to simple Kanians keeping their modest households, and stocked up on freshly baked, extraordinarily tasty bread. They didn't care about the feud between Tensess and Nezeb, or about the war between the League and the Empire...

Now ghosts hold sway there. As before, they go about their business: catching fish, hunting, grinding flour. And they were not at all glad to see either me or my crew. We barely got away.

I'm at a loss! What evil has appeared in the Silent Hills? Who cursed those poor people?

If you have the courage to take up the challenge of this riddle, follow my advice. Look for the cause of the Silent Hills' woes in the dark forest! The peasants always gave that place a wide berth. Perhaps one of them broke the age-old order and woke the evil slumbering there. Obstacles will surely stand in your way that you will have to overcome to reach the source of the evil. Remember that you will not be able to cleanse the island without fighting its ghostly inhabitants. That is the pain you will have to go through. Know that you bring them not death but deliverance from Darkness.

Bosses: Tsar Pike, Elder Miller, the Bane of Silent Hills.

Long ago honest folk jokingly called one distant district the Far-Far-Away Kingdom. It was a real backwater: a rider couldn't get through, nor a man on foot. A wall of trees — for hundreds of versts! And this land was ruled by a wise guardian — the living soul of the forest. She did not favor wicked travelers, but for good ones the path through the thicket unrolled of its own accord.

After the Cataclysm only a pitiful scrap of that forest remained. And the guardian, they say, survived — she watches over her domain as in the old days. Every traveler can count on shelter and rest under the canopy of the ancient trees. But Light forbid anyone should harm the local animals! It is said more than one poachers' vessel has vanished without a trace near the Isle of Far-Far-Away!

Bosses: Forest Spirit, Veleslav Dubov, Blackmarin, Forest Guardian.

If the idea of lazing about on sultry tropical shores doesn't appeal to you, we suggest you visit Triplefield! The Kanian town of Triplefield is a historical monument to the friendship of peoples! Here the Kanians and the elves of House de Doucer have long walked hand in hand, inspired by the brightest ideals. Forward — to a world of universal prosperity and Great Beauty!

Alas, the town's cultural and administrative center is currently closed owing to the war between werewolves and vampires. All the local elves of House de Doucer have turned into the latter. But never mind — in the south of the island the surviving Kanians have rebuilt a small village where you will surely be able to find a good guide.

During your journey around the island you can visit the enchanting enclave of the fallen elves. Their leader, Alister de Doucer, will receive you in his chambers and demonstrate the heights he has reached over long years in the art of training bats. His servants will consider it an honor to delight your ears with harp music and conversations about the beauty of twilight at this time of year.

Don't miss the chance to visit the ethnic community of werewolves, too. Only in the local cave can you hear songs performed by a moonlit choir of men and wolves. The pack leader, Mstislav Ferocious, will be glad to tell you old tales of grey wolves, and will also demonstrate stunts with fire in human and wolf form in turn!

Of course, it's worth seeing the part of the island once visited by the great Kanian inquisitor Alex Gordev. In the recent past this holy man wanted to rid the elves of the vampiric curse. The power of faith blazed brightly in his eyes, ready to burn away the corruption with one mighty blow of the Light... But something went wrong. Instead, the inquisitor himself turned into a terrifying undead, and the same fate befell all his guards.

Bosses: Alister de Doucer, Mstislav Ferocious, Milava Troepolskaya, Alex Gordev.

"No minerals. No water. No vegetation. Inhabited by mechanoids" — in most ship's logs this island has not earned a more detailed description. They say that while the cultists and mechanoids of Irdrich were fighting the combined army of the League and the Empire, a rusty barge with Tep's former slaves quietly slipped away from the shore. Evidently the old lord no longer met the fugitives' quality requirements.

But the habit of obedience stayed with the mechanoids, and demand always creates supply. They chose an inconspicuous corner of the Astral and set about building an artificial intelligence — their new deity. Such a project requires an enormous amount of resources, which is why the islet is melting away before your eyes. Ship captains should be careful — after all, astral vessels are an excellent source of valuable materials and equipment.

Bosses: Fill-o-Matic, Nomarkh Megavolt, Negus Augment, Integral.

Since time immemorial mortals have challenged the Gods. Some daredevils really do manage to succeed and win fame for the ages. But most meet an inglorious end, or even something worse. Nihaz, for instance, created a whole astral island — the Jail. There go the Sparks of those who dared to get under the Lord's divine feet.

The prison allod is guarded without breaks or days off by guards armed to the teeth. The island is considered secret, so visitors are not especially welcome.

Bosses: Bloody Executioner, Farakh, the Overlord's Punishment, Provost.

Duck River Run is a calm and picturesque place. The folk who live there are simple, warm-hearted and friendly. But here's the trouble — their kindness backfired on them. When an orc gang attacked the island, the locals could not fight them off.

Those bandits are from the Empire. Each of them faced a term in the camps back home, so they stole a ship and took flight. So replenishing supplies off the shores of Duck River Run is no longer safe.

Bosses: Torch the Daring, Haze the Daring, Rod the Daring, Chopper the Daring.

The Ravine of Shadows? I've heard of it, heard of it. I haven't been there myself, I won't lie. But a traveling Priden told me that long, long ago — so long that even their Voices barely remember when — a huge chunk broke away from Howlem, with some temple on it. The Priden believe they angered the First Ones and were punished by them.

About the curse of the First Ones I can't say, but I've heard from astral pirates of a huge mountain in the Astral with old ruins towering on its summit. Gentlemen of fortune tried to plunder something valuable there and barely escaped with their lives. They whispered that their own shadows came to life and began killing left and right. And when all that pirate rabble scattered in every direction, ghosts — of men or of beasts, who knows — stood in their way with weapons in their hands, and not one of them reached the ruins alive. Those who managed to dash back to the ship fled that island under full sail. So I reckon that if it was a curse, it still haunts anyone who dares to enter that Ravine...

Bosses: Forgotten, Maas-Risa the Bedazzling, Saad-Brok the Stormbringer, Shoom-Kagat the Black-Handed.

This island belongs to Nomarkh Iblis — an oligarch and inventor. He's a rich man, well known, but not much respected. He's far too fond of inventing schemes to cheat his partners instead of weapons. Only this last time he picked the wrong target: he had the gall to swindle Yasker himself. Yasker wouldn't stand for the insult, and as soon as his scouts found the island, he sent a whole battalion there. How it all ended, I don't know. Nohow, I think: the imperial soldiers are strong, but a factory stuffed to the roof with weapons can't be taken at a rush either. We Leaguers have no business there — except perhaps to watch the show from afar. Want to bet? I'll wager ten gold that the Imperials won't manage it!

Bosses: Yasskul Samekh, Modified Orc, Ghost of Yaver Khess, Polytoc Hexnut.

There is an island in the Astral that can only be called an island with a stretch. On the one hand — big, well-shaped, there's even a little village nestled on it. On the other — it's not an allod at all, but a large floating turtle. The traveler never objected to her passengers, so they lived relatively well. Until recently.

They say the turtle island has been seized by demon worshippers. They have killed the local inhabitants and are trying to bend their drifting home to their evil will. And if they succeed, great trouble awaits the League and the Empire.

Bosses: Tikhon Yezhov, Hardshell, Gostemil Zalesky, Velerad Zalesky.

Even seasoned astral captains shudder on hearing of this allod. A dark and inhospitable place, once the domain of the elves of House de Blizare, today it lies in gloom. Its present masters are demons, which means that a journey to the dark allod will be a real ordeal even for the most desperate travelers.

Bosses: Gryzl, Bonegrinder, Hornbearer, Sparky.

The Plague City includes several quarters: the slums of the poor, the merchant, craftsmen's and central districts, and the sewers. It is impossible to get onto the streets through the main gates, since the plague doctors have closed the city under quarantine. Astronauts have to make their way into the sewers, where countless plague rats and spawn of the pestilence live.

Having fought their way through the sewer pipes, the heroes find themselves in the poor districts: hunger, poverty, countless stray street animals and looters. The atmosphere of the streets is truly spellbinding. Here too lives a gang of demolitionists led by Long Arm.

Beyond the poor quarters comes the craftsmen's quarter. Here the players watch clashes between looters and the plague doctors and "cleaners," and take part in these clashes themselves. Fighting their way through the narrow streets, the players come out onto a spacious square.

Here Yaver Brand, commander of the cleaners' squad, has set up.

Beyond the craftsmen's quarter and the merchant quarter comes the main square, where the heroes must stop three warlocks, get into the main tower and defeat the Devastator himself.

Bosses: Hur the Boiling, Long Arm, Yaver Brand, Devastator.

I know that place. Only I strongly advise you not to fly there!

On that island there's a whole village of religious fanatics. Unwashed peasants, who until recently were meekly growing turnips for the Kanian soldiery, have got above themselves. They've renounced faith in the Light, not to mention veneration of the saints Nezeb and Skrakan, and worship some kind of nature spirits. And in charge of them is the volkhv Jaromir. It was he, that bearded lunatic, who stirred all the peasants to revolt! He's completely addled the village men's heads with his tales about the faith of their ancestors, the greatness of ancient Kania, glorious Traditions... No, honoring traditions is sacred. But with some sense! We're building mana stations and underground metros, the League is treading on our heels in industrial development, and they're still living in the last millennium. A wild people, in a word — not like us, the enlightened citizens of the great Empire.

So if the road leads you to Clear Mountain, get ready to fight the whole village at once. And the local bogatyrs as well — Alexei, Ivan and Vladislav, great hulking brutes: step out of line and they'll pound you into the ground up to your ears. But if you manage to defeat Jaromir himself, maybe the peasants will come to their senses and stop grabbing every stranger and throwing him into the Astral...

Bosses: Aunt Agafya, Vladislav the Cruel, Prokopy, Jaromir.
Bosses: Sylvan, Kodo the Silent and Nigan the Silent, Sentry, Veliyar.
Bosses: Firebliz the Righteous, Svetlana Pravdina, Crucifier, Kirill Pravdin, the Guise-Stealer.
Bosses: Mikhail Blankstare, Artem Ostankin, George Podpalin, Hungry Demon, Megalit.
Bosses: Armando de Doucer, Poisonous Trap, Darksoul Leader, Purger Fire Thrower, Meat Golem.
Bosses: Trap, Asyka, Marcel de Doucer, Daring Family, Miroslav Kramolsky.
Bosses: Fleshwither, Inevitable Death, Ravager, Vur'tazz the Ravager, Soul Sucker.
Bosses: Vissarion Arhivin, Yasskul Ktash, Astral Overlord, Gorluxor, Demon of Decay.
Bosses: Ushan, Rottenfang, Cobweb Spider, Shadow, Zinovy Gorsky.
